We want to find the smallest positive integer $x$ satisfying the system of congruences:
1. $x \equiv 3 \pmod{13}$
2. $x \equiv 11 \pmod{16}$
3. $x \equiv 5 \pmod{17}$

From the second congruence, $x = 16k + 11$. Substituting into the third congruence:
$16k + 11 \equiv 5 \pmod{17}$
$-k - 6 \equiv 5 \pmod{17}$
$k \equiv -11 \equiv 6 \pmod{17}$

So $k = 17m + 6$, which gives:
$x = 16(17m + 6) + 11 = 272m + 107$

Now substituting this into the first congruence:
$272m + 107 \equiv 3 \pmod{13}$
Since $272 \equiv -1 \pmod{13}$ and $107 \equiv 3 \pmod{13}$:
$-m + 3 \equiv 3 \pmod{13}$
$m \equiv 0 \pmod{13}$

The smallest non-negative integer is $m = 0$, giving:
$x = 107$

FINAL: 107
